items.headline: Higher threshold for top income tax rate
items.summary: President Dissanayake said the 2028 Budget will raise the monthly income level at which the top 36% PAYE rate applies to Rs. 500,000, and pledged that capital spending will not be cut. He also pushed back against public sector pay protests.

items.headline: Netherlands to return two Kandyan guns
items.summary: Two 18th-century rampart guns taken from the Kandyan Kingdom during Dutch rule and held at Amsterdam's Rijksmuseum will be handed back to Sri Lanka. Research linked them to the 1765 war with the Dutch East India Company; return arrangements will follow.

items.headline: Rs. 181m hashish found in Malaysian parcels
items.summary: Customs opened three unclaimed parcels from Malaysia at a Peliyagoda warehouse and found about 18 kg of hashish. The drugs were handed to the Police Narcotics Bureau for further investigation.

items.headline: Minister urges one-third cut in paddy cultivation
items.summary: Agriculture Minister K. D. Lal Kantha said rice farming should shrink by at least a third because of surplus stocks and weak demand. The government is looking at exports before the Maha harvest and pushing farmers toward other crops.

items.headline: Bay of Bengal low-pressure advisory
items.summary: Fishing and naval communities were told to stay alert from November 29 to December 3, as a low-pressure area may form over the southeast Bay of Bengal around November 30. Forecasters see only a low chance of it becoming a depression.

items.headline: Third salary hike phase set for January
items.summary: PM Harini Amarasuriya told teacher and principal unions the third phase of the public sector pay increase will take effect in January 2027. A Salary and Pension Commission has been appointed to address anomalies.

items.headline: Mitra Shakti-XII exercise ends
items.summary: The 12th India–Sri Lanka joint army exercise wrapped up at Maduru Oya after nearly two weeks, involving more than 350 troops from both sides.

items.headline: Ceylon Cinnamon gets national GI status
items.summary: The Export Development Board received Sri Lanka's first national Geographical Indication certificate, for Ceylon Cinnamon, after nearly a decade of work. Officials aim to lift cinnamon exports to US$1 billion by 2030.

items.headline: CSE ends lower
items.summary: The ASPI fell 0.33% to 21,244.91 as decliners outnumbered gainers, though foreign investors were small net buyers.

items.headline: First national ECMO centre opens in Galle
items.summary: Galle National Hospital opened a three-bed centre for patients with severe heart or lung failure, along with a simulation unit to train medical staff.

items.headline: Kinniya bridge under construction
items.summary: A Rs. 1,050 million Saudi-funded bridge across the Kurinchakerny lagoon is due in 2027, five years after a ferry capsizing there killed eight people. A free ferry runs meanwhile.

items.headline: Cyclone Ditwah, one year on
items.summary: A year after Ditwah killed more than 650 people, nearly all relief allowances have been paid and 1,615 families resettled, but rebuilding remains far from complete.

items.headline: Tamil Nadu opens homes for Sri Lankan Tamils
items.summary: Chief Minister Vijay inaugurated 148 houses at a Krishnagiri rehabilitation camp and raised monthly cash aid for about 56,600 Sri Lankan Tamil refugees.
